gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-thai-loop: Classic in feel, Edo SZ stands its lowercase up like cast iron capitals, one constant stroke throughout. Noto Sans Thai Looped brings tall, bold-looking lowercase with spacious curve terminals.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Cultural weight up top: Edo SZ has cast-iron-capital stature in its lowercase. Noto Sans Tifinagh sits below with rounded, inviting letters whose inflated bowls fill the line, while the heading's single stroke width stays constant.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Tubing, bent into letters: Edo SZ keeps one constant stroke from end to end. Noto Sans Tirhuta then lets text run on with terminals cut back to leave wide gaps and a dominant x-height, so paragraphs feel open.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Approachable chalk-arc openness lives in the body, while Edo SZ up top keeps a unit-width stroke throughout its tall lowercase. Noto Sans Ugaritic leaves little gap between x-height and cap height.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-vai: Strokes like bent copper pipe give Edo SZ its look, all tubular and constant in width. Noto Sans Vai lays words down as solid blocks beneath it, with generous space between curve ends and stems.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Edo SZ is a plain stripe of constant ink, with lowercase built to the stature of cast iron capitals. And Noto Sans Vithkuqi brings open throats and a barely-there step from capital to lowercase.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Flat as a fineliner line, Edo SZ stands its lowercase up with cast iron stature and a single constant stroke. Noto Sans Wancho would read hulking and chalky down a whole page.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-yi: Edo SZ gives its diagonals the full weight of its uprights. Noto Sans Yi sits underneath with a deep lowercase midsection and rounds left unlatched like a hook, against that stern stripe.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square brings a soaring x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. But Edo SZ, with bowl outlines that never swell or thin, leaves the text to carry paragraphs smoothly.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-traditional-nu: Edo SZ draws rounded strokes like cut lengths of cord, with lowercase of cast iron stature. But Noto Traditional Nushu does the quieter work, its broad-nibbed stroke never curling shut and its bowls filling the line.
